section_summary: This section contains correspondence about American and British holders of Japanese government and municipal bonds. The State Department explains its limited role in protecting private investors, directs American holders toward claims against vested Japanese assets, and tells the British Embassy that existing law excludes British debt claims against those assets.

people.name: A. N. Overby
people.role: Special Assistant to the Secretary of the Treasury

people.name: James C. Corliss
people.role: Assistant Chief, Division of Financial Affairs

subfiles.title: Inquiry about protection of Japanese bondholders
subfiles.about: Pappy asks whether the government is protecting American holders of Japanese bonds or whether they should form a protective committee.
subfiles.summary: Pappy seeks advice on protecting American investors holding Japanese Imperial Government bonds.

subfiles.title: Treasury referral of T. Kimura's bond inquiry
subfiles.about: The Treasury forwards Kimura's inquiry about servicing Japanese government obligations for State Department action.
subfiles.summary: Treasury forwards Kimura's inquiry for appropriate action.

subfiles.title: Government Information Service referral notice
subfiles.from: Government Information Service, Office of Government Reports
subfiles.about: A standard notice explains that the attached letter has been forwarded to the agency with jurisdiction.
subfiles.summary: Standard interagency referral notice; the writer was not informed.

subfiles.title: T. Kimura's inquiry about the Japanese franc loan
subfiles.about: Kimura asks about coupons and interest on bonds of the Imperial Japanese Government's 1910 franc loan.
subfiles.summary: Kimura refers to a newspaper notice and asks about interest due on his bonds.

subfiles.title: Reply to T. Kimura on Japanese franc-loan bonds
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: State explains its position on foreign bonds and requests proof of Kimura's American citizenship.
subfiles.summary: State says a definitive answer is unavailable, records Kimura's information, requests citizenship evidence, and encloses naturalization and claims materials.

subfiles.title: Instruction to deliver reply to T. Kimura
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, Calgary
subfiles.about: State asks the Calgary consulate to transmit its reply to Kimura unless it sees an objection.
subfiles.summary: Requests consular delivery of the enclosed reply to Kimura.

subfiles.title: British request for equal access to Japanese bond-service funds
subfiles.about: Britain asks that its bondholders be allowed to claim against vested funds deposited for servicing five Japanese bond issues.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy seeks equal treatment for British holders despite the passed June 1 claims deadline.

subfiles.title: State response on British debt claims
subfiles.about: State explains that the extended filing deadline does not make British bondholders' debt claims allowable under existing law.
subfiles.summary: Although the claims deadline was extended to September 2, State says statutory eligibility rules exclude British holders' debt claims.

subfiles.title: Reply to Mary Lewis Ervin about a Japanese bond
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: State explains its policy toward Japanese dollar bonds and identifies possible representation and claims procedures.
subfiles.summary: State records Ervin's bond information, describes the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council and its communication with occupation authorities, and notes uncertainty about a peace settlement. It advises American holders that claims against vested assets may be filed with the Office of Alien Property by September 2, 1947.

subfiles.title: Mary Lewis Ervin's Japanese bond inquiry
subfiles.about: Ervin writes about her $1,000 bond from the Imperial Japanese Government External Loan of 1924.
subfiles.summary: Ervin reports her Japanese external-loan bond to the Department.
